[image: Ballots go in the mail across Washington today. Vote the whole ballot, top to bottom, and return it early – by mail with no stamp needed, or at any drop box. Then check in with two people you know and make sure they do the same. Not registered yet? You can still register online or by mail through October 26, or in person through Election Day, November 3. VoteWA.gov]

[image: Ballots go in the mail by October 16, and Spokane County's may arrive early. Watch your mailbox! Here's how to help: 1. Fill it out top to bottom and return it early. 2. Post a photo of your sealed envelope (never your marked ballot) with #FlipWA05. 3. Tag three friends and ask if theirs has arrived. Dem clubs and Indivisible groups: please share this with your members. Every early ballot frees up volunteers to reach the voters who haven't heard from us yet.]

[image: Spokane Public Radio asked me what I would do first. Two things. Bring costs down by restoring a predictable trade regime: reset tariffs to where they were in January 2025 and fully restore USMCA, so businesses and families can plan again. End the war with Iran. It is expensive, and we are all seeing it at the gas pump. Whether we go to war is Congress's decision, and five times Michael Baumgartner voted not to even have that discussion. Listen to the full interview: https://www.spokanepublicradio.org/regional-news/2026-10-01/congressional-candidate-carmela-conroy-talks-affordability-ai-iran-war]
[image: The Spokesman-Review lined up where Michael Baumgartner and I stand on the issues, side by side. Read it before you fill out your ballot. The choice is clear. https://f.mtr.cool/azr57im1u1]

[image: Three weeks to go — and this campaign is moving! This week’s Conroy Connection is a look at what’s happening on the ground as we head into the final stretch: volunteers stepping up in new ways, neighbors organizing, recent press coverage, new endorsements, upcoming events, and plenty of opportunities to get involved. The big moments matter, but so do the little ones — the phone calls, the doors knocked, the signs waved, the late-night emails, and all the work people do when nobody is watching. Take a look at what the campaign has been up to and what’s ahead as we move toward Election Day!]
